problems: The caption's 'cut lines', 'dipped it' and 'fired it' never appear: all 16 storyboard frames show the same finished jug standing on sand while the camera slowly circles it. No cutting, no dip, no kiln and no heat at any point.
'The glaze flowed while hot' is not shown. The jug is identical in every frame, so nothing flows, drips or changes.

'Its colour is how thick it ended up' cannot be seen. In the 25/50/75% frames the jug is one flat, matte olive-brown all over. There is no pooling in the incised lines, no thinning at the rim or shoulder and no gloss, so it does not read as glazed at all and could just as well be bare clay.
The incised lines are faint thin grooves that only show up at full size (25% and 50% frames). In the storyboard they are barely visible.

Late in the film (storyboard rows 3–4, 75% frame) a big pale-green plant leaf swings into the frame and covers the jug's rim and the top right of the jug, so the subject is partly hidden for the last third.
The plant beside the jug is coarse and faceted, with broken-looking flat-shaded chunks (top right of the 25% and 50% frames). The scene looks unfinished.
The film is 9 s of a motionless object with a drifting camera. Nothing happens, so a viewer who doesn't know the island has nothing to follow.
posts.critique: The caption tells a whole process (cutting, dipping, firing, glaze flowing and thickness showing as colour), but the film only shows a finished, flat-coloured jug on sand from an orbiting camera, so almost everything the caption claims is missing. A leaf covering the jug for the last stretch and the broken-looking plant make it weaker still.
